definitions.explanation: A meeting conducted remotely using video and audio technology, allowing participants in different locations to see and hear each other.

examples.japanese: テレビ{会議|かいぎ}で{参加|さんか}する。
{海外|かいがい}の{支社|ししゃ}とテレビ{会議|かいぎ}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: We held a video conference with the overseas branch office.

examples.japanese: リモートワークが{普及|ふきゅう}してから、{毎日|まいにち}のようにテレビ{会議|かいぎ}が{入|はい}るようになった。
examples.english: Since remote work became widespread, I've ended up having video conferences almost every day.

notes:
A compound of テレビ (television/video) and {会議|かいぎ} (meeting, conference). This term became especially common during and after the COVID-19 pandemic as remote work became mainstream.

USAGE:
- Used with を{行|おこな}う (to hold), に{参加|さんか}する (to participate in), or を{開|ひら}く (to open/start)
- Often shortened in casual speech or used interchangeably with newer terms like Web{会議|かいぎ} or オンライン{会議|かいぎ}
- テレビ{会議|かいぎ} originally implied specialized corporate systems, but now broadly covers any video meeting

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- テレビ{会議|かいぎ}を{行|おこな}う: to hold a video conference
- テレビ{会議|かいぎ}システム: video conferencing system
- テレビ{会議|かいぎ}{用|よう}: for video conferencing
- テレビ{会議|かいぎ}で{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせ: meeting via video conference

SIMILAR WORDS:
- Web{会議|かいぎ}: web conference — emphasizes internet-based meetings; the more modern term for tools like Zoom
- オンライン{会議|かいぎ}: online meeting — generic term for any internet-based meeting
- {電話|でんわ}{会議|かいぎ}: telephone conference, conference call — audio only, no video
